title: The Unwritten Contract of Cloud-based Elastic Solid-State Drives
problem: Despite widespread cloud adoption, the performance characteristics and suitability of Elastic SSDs (ESSDs) as local SSD replacements remain uncharacterized, leaving cloud storage users uncertain about deployment decisions.
method: Characterizes two production ESSDs from AWS and Alibaba Cloud through comprehensive benchmarking, identifies counter-intuitive performance patterns, and derives design implications for cloud software optimization to exploit ESSD-specific characteristics.

title: Design and Technology Co-optimization Utilizing Flip-FET (FFET) Standard Cells
problem: CFET-based standard cells require excessive tap-cell overhead in FEOL to enable backside interconnect routing, hindering efficient use of BEOL backside wiring in sub-3nm nodes.
method: FFET (Flip-FET) flips the lower FET in CFET to enable direct pin accessibility on both BEOL sides without tap-cells. DTCO uses: (1) synthesizing multiple FFET cells with diverse pin distributions, (2) tap-cell-avoiding placement optimization, (3) frontside/backside wire rebalancing.

title: Lumina: Real-Time Neural Rendering by Exploiting Computational Redundancy
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) neural rendering is computationally demanding for mobile SoCs, with high rasterization costs and redundant computation across temporally-coherent frames preventing real-time performance.
method: Lumina integrates two algorithmic optimizations: S2 (Spatial-temporal Skipping) exploits temporal coherence to skip recomputation of unchanged Gaussian contributions across frames, and RC (Radiance Caching) caches intermediate color integration values to reduce rasterization frequency. The LuminCore hardware accelerator is co-designed with these algorithms to efficiently support cache lookups and address rasterization inefficiencies inherent in the standard 3DGS pipeline on mobile hardware.

title: A 28nm Multimode Multiband RF Transceiver with Harmonic-Rejection TX and Spur-Avoidance RX Supporting LTE Cat1bis
problem: Cellular IoT applications (LTE Cat1bis) demand cost-effective RF transceivers supporting diverse data rates and frequency bands. Die size, packaging, and bill-of-materials (BoM) cost are critical adoption barriers. Traditional transceivers incur high silicon area overhead for multi-band support and complex TX/RX filtering.
method: A 28nm CMOS multimode multiband RF transceiver integrates harmonic-rejection transmitter architecture reducing external filter requirements and spur-avoidance RX front-end enabling simpler filtering. Multiband support via tunable filtering and integrated LNA/mixer/IF stages minimize external components while supporting LTE Cat1bis protocols.

title: 20.7 A 384-Site Chip Platform for Biochemical Applications with Individual Site Precision Temperature Control
problem: Biochemical processors require independent temperature control on multiple sites (384-site platform) for parallel PCR, gene assembly, and other thermally-tuned reactions, but silicon substrate thermal conductivity prevents efficient local isolation and precise sensing.
method: 384-site chip platform using thermal isolation structures and independent local temperature sensors/heaters per site, overcoming substrate thermal conductivity to achieve precise individual-site temperature control for biochemical applications.

title: QR-Map: A Map-Based Approach to Quantum Circuit Abstraction for Qubit Reuse Optimization
problem: Identifying optimal qubit reuse opportunities in quantum circuits via mid-circuit measurements is NP-hard in the general case; existing frameworks either suffer from exponential search complexity or produce non-optimal results due to non-deterministic heuristics.
method: QR-Map abstracts computational dependencies by extracting and aligning two-qubit gates into a map structure, making dependency detection deterministic and tractable. The framework identifies qubit reuse opportunities by analyzing these aligned gate maps, ensuring qubit savings without introducing excessive idle time. It jointly optimizes gate serialization depth and crosstalk reduction, balancing circuit fidelity with hardware constraints through a deterministic, polynomial-time map-based search.

title: 33.3 A 125-to-170GHz Power-Efficient Phase Shifter in SiGe BiCMOS with Outphasing Gain and Phase Corrections
problem: Sub-THz phased-array transceivers for high-resolution radar and wireless communications require broadband, power-efficient phase shifters spanning 125–170GHz. Traditional phase-shifter architectures struggle with phase accuracy, amplitude imbalance, and power efficiency at such high frequencies in silicon technologies.
method: Power-efficient phase shifter leveraging outphasing technique for simultaneous gain and phase correction. Outphasing decomposes phase-amplitude modulation into orthogonal constant-amplitude paths, enabling efficient RF amplification with minimal power. Integrated gain adjustment and phase correction compensate for process/temperature variations. SiGe BiCMOS technology provides high-frequency performance suitable for 125–170GHz operation while maintaining integration density.

title: Property-driven Parallel Symbolic Model Checking of LTL
problem: Symbolic model checking for LTL properties faces state explosion challenge and lacks efficient parallelization of nested fixpoint calculations; most existing work focuses only on reachability or safety, not full LTL with fairness constraints.
method: Proposes property-driven parallel symbolic model checking using a fair model state labeling function that partitions nested fixpoint calculations across the product automaton combining the model and property Büchi automaton. This enables distributed computation of the fixpoint while maintaining correctness under LTL fairness conditions.

title: 13.5 An 18.5µW/qubit Cryo-CMOS Charge-Readout IC Demonstrating QAM Multiplexing for Spin Qubits
problem: Scaling spin qubits to thousands of devices requires simultaneous readout with minimal per-qubit power consumption and footprint, but existing FDM reflectometry and integrator schemes are limited by bulky inductors or poor scaling to large arrays.
method: Cryo-CMOS charge-readout IC using quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) multiplexing to read multiple spin qubits on a single carrier frequency, eliminating bulky inductors via capacitive-feedback transimpedance amplifier architecture.

title: An 85-to-230VAC to 3.3-to-4.6VDc 1.52W Capacitor-Drop Sigma-Floating-SC AC-DC Converter with 81.3% Peak Efficiency
problem: IoT and smart-home devices require high-efficiency, low-cost, compact non-isolated AC-DC converters for AC mains to battery-voltage output with large voltage conversion ratios (VCR). Traditional inductive switching converters are bulky; linear regulators are inefficient. Switched-capacitor approaches have poor output power scaling and lack voltage regulation.
method: A sigma-floating switched-capacitor (SC) architecture with capacitor-drop AC-DC topology and three-mode active rectifier regulation. Capacitive division blocks high AC voltage using series capacitors, reducing stress on integrated converter stages. A semi-active or three-mode active rectifier adjusts current to maintain regulated DC output while minimizing idle-phase losses compared to prior two-phase designs.

title: FactorHD: A Hyperdimensional Computing Model for Multi-Object Multi-Class Representation and Factorization
problem: Existing HDC models struggle to represent and factorize complex multi-object class-subclass relations; they suffer from superposition catastrophe and information loss when handling multiple objects simultaneously.
method: FactorHD encodes each object with a symbolic memorization clause to preserve multi-object information, avoiding superposition catastrophe. Factorization algorithm selectively eliminates redundant classes by identifying the memorization clause of the target class.

title: Photonic Interconnect for Accelerated Computing Celestial AI Photonic Fabric Module - The world's first SoC with in-die Optical IO
problem: AI accelerator systems require on-die optical I/O to overcome electrical interconnect bandwidth and power density limitations, enabling scalable many-accelerator configurations.
method: Celestial AI implements monolithic optical I/O on a single SoC die combining photonic modulators, detectors, and waveguides with electrical compute logic to enable direct optical communication.

title: Reuse-Aware Compilation for Zoned Quantum Architectures Based on Neutral Atoms
problem: Neutral-atom quantum computers use heterogeneous zoned architectures (storage, entangling, readout zones), and compiling quantum circuits for them requires efficiently managing qubit movement between zones to minimize fidelity-degrading data movement overhead.
method: ZAC (Zoned Architecture Compiler) introduces qubit reuse as a core optimization: qubits already in the entanglement zone are kept there if an immediate entangling gate is pending, avoiding round-trip movement to storage. ZAC additionally introduces novel data placement strategies that anticipate future gate scheduling needs, a new instruction scheduling algorithm for zoned operations, a flexible specification language for diverse zoned architectures, and ZAIR, an intermediate representation capturing zoned-architecture-specific constraints. The compiler is evaluated on circuits showing 22x fidelity improvement over monolithic architectures.

title: M-ANT: Efficient Low-bit Group Quantization for LLMs via Mathematically Adaptive Numerical Type
problem: Existing adaptive data types for LLM group quantization provide adaptivity at the tensor level, but small quantization groups within the same tensor exhibit markedly different distributions that tensor-level formats cannot accommodate. Additionally, dynamically generated KV caches require efficient real-time quantization that existing approaches do not support well.
method: MANT defines a mathematically adaptive numeric type with a flexible encoding paradigm covering a wider range of data distributions than prior adaptive types. A hardware framework assigns the appropriate MANT variant to each quantization group dynamically. A dedicated processing element (PE) fuses decoding and computation, and a real-time quantization unit handles dynamic KV cache quantization. These PEs are integrated into a systolic array, unifying weight and KV cache quantization in a single datapath.

title: An 18.5nF-Input-Range PM-SAR-Hybrid Capacitance-to-Digital Converter Achieving 6.1µs Conversion Time at 18.1pF Input Capacitance
problem: Capacitive sensors require wide-input-range (>10nF), fast-conversion (<10µs), high-resolution CDCs. SAR and ΔΣM CDCs offer energy efficiency but suffer from limited input range due to analog saturation. Period-modulation (PM) CDCs achieve wide range but incur long conversion times counting oscillation periods.
method: PM-SAR-Hybrid CDC combining period modulation (for wide range via time-domain operation) with SAR conversion (for fast resolution), eliminating saturation limits while achieving sub-10µs conversion. SAR post-processing counts/resolves PM oscillation cycles efficiently.

title: MDPeek: Breaking Balanced Branches in SGX with Memory Disambiguation Unit Side Channels
problem: Intel SGX enclaves are believed to be protected against control-flow side-channel attacks when software defenses balance branch execution paths; this paper discovers that the Memory Disambiguation Unit (MDU) inside modern Intel CPUs leaks information even through these balanced branches, creating a previously unknown side channel.
method: MDPeek exploits the Memory Disambiguation Unit, a microarchitectural structure that speculatively allows or stalls dependent loads/stores based on address aliasing predictions. By crafting enclave access patterns that cause the MDU to make different predictions for secret-dependent branches (even when those branches are balanced at the instruction level), the attacker can observe MDU state changes through timing differences in a co-located spy process. The attack methodology reverse-engineers MDU behavior in Intel CPUs and demonstrates end-to-end information leakage from SGX enclaves.
